Empirical Research Plan: 1979–1983 NLSY Cohorts and the 1982 Termination of the Social-Security Student Benefit  

======================================================================
1. Identification Strategy
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Method: Difference-in-Differences with an embedded “triple-difference” (DDD).

• Dimension 1 (time): Pre-policy cohorts (high-school seniors 1979–1981) vs. Post-policy cohorts (seniors 1982–1983).  
• Dimension 2 (eligibility): Youths whose father died before age 18 (= potential beneficiaries) vs. youths with a living father (= never eligible).  
• Dimension 3 (inherent eligibility vs. secular trends): DDD nets out (i) permanent level differences between orphans and non-orphans and (ii) economy-wide time shocks common to both groups.

Why appropriate?
– The program ended abruptly in May-1982, producing a sharp discontinuity by high-school graduating cohort that is plausibly exogenous to youths’ schooling decisions.  
– Father-death before age 18 is pre-determined relative to the policy and to college enrollment choices.  
– NLSY follows both eligible and ineligible individuals before and after the cutoff, allowing the construction of clean counterfactual trends.

Event-study graphs of cohort dummies interacted with orphan status will complement the DID, testing for parallel pre-trends and visualizing dynamic responses.

======================================================================
2. Treatment and Control
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
  Treat_i = 1{Father deceased before age 18 AND Senior-year ∈ 1979–1981}.  
  These individuals could still receive benefits conditional on college enrollment.

Control groups  
  a. Internal DID: Orphans in 1982–1983 cohorts who suddenly lost eligibility.  
  b. Non-orphans in all cohorts to purge macro time shocks (DDD).

Treatment timing / event date  
  Policy announcement & enactment: December 1981.  
  Effective loss of eligibility: May 1, 1982.  
  Cohort classification: Senior-year ≤1981 = “pre”; ≥1982 = “post”.

No running variable is required; we exploit discrete cohort exposure rather than a continuous cutoff.

======================================================================
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
----------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel-Trends (DDD version): In the absence of the 1982 termination, the change in college outcomes for orphans relative to non-orphans would have been the same for 1979-1981 cohorts as for 1982-1983 cohorts.  
  Plausibility: Short window (five senior-year classes) reduces risk of divergent trends; no other contemporaneous policy uniquely affecting orphans’ college attendance is known.

A2. Exogeneity of Father Death to Schooling Trends: Father mortality before age 18 is effectively random with respect to impending 1982 policy change and schooling choices at ages 18-22.  
  Plausibility: Death events occurred years earlier; cannot be manipulated in anticipation.

A3. Stable Treatment Definition: Eligibility rules did not otherwise change differentially for the study groups during 1979-1983.  
  Plausibility: The only relevant change was the outright elimination of benefits.

======================================================================
4. Threats to Identification and Mitigation
----------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Differential economic shocks for orphaned families (e.g., recession-related income shocks 1982).  
   Mitigation:  
   • Include family-income controls measured in senior year.  
   • Add state-by-cohort fixed effects to absorb regional macro shocks.

T2. Measurement error in father-death variable (misreporting survival status).  
   Mitigation:  
   • Cross-check with parental survival status recorded in multiple NLSY rounds.  
   • Estimate attenuated-bias bounds; show robustness to dropping uncertain cases.

T3. Concurrent changes in other student aid (e.g., Pell Grant expansions in early 1980s).  
   Mitigation:  
   • These changes affected both orphans and non-orphans; hence differenced out in DDD.  
   • Add interaction of Pell-grant generosity (state×year) with cohort to verify insensitivity.

======================================================================
5. R Code Outline
----------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# 0. Packages ---------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)
library(fixest)      # fast fixed-effects OLS
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load data --------------------------------------------------------
nlsy <- fread("nlsy_1979_1988_extract.csv")   # hypothetical file

# 2. Variable construction -------------------------------------------
nlsy[, senior_year := year_hs_senior]           # given
nlsy[, cohort_pre := as.integer(senior_year <= 1981)]
nlsy[, post      := 1 - cohort_pre]             # 1 if 1982–83
nlsy[, father_dead := as.integer(father_died_before18 == 1)]

# Treatment indicator for simple DID
nlsy[, treat := father_dead * cohort_pre]

# Outcomes
nlsy[, enroll   := as.integer(ever_fulltime_college == 1)]
nlsy[, hgc_23   := highest_grade_completed_age23]
nlsy[, hgc_28   := highest_grade_completed_age28]

# Controls
controls <- c("afqt_pct", "log_family_income",
              "mother_hs", "mother_ba", "father_hs", "father_ba",
              "black", "hispanic", "female", "family_size",
              "state_residence", "age_at_senior")

# 3. Main DDD regression ---------------------------------------------
formula_main <- as.formula(
  paste0("enroll ~ father_dead*post + ",          # interaction is coefficient of interest
         paste(controls, collapse = " + "),
         " | state_residence + senior_year"))     # 2-way FE

did_enroll <- feols(formula_main, data = nlsy, weights = ~nlsy_weight,
                    cluster = ~senior_year)
summary(did_enroll)

# 4. Years of schooling at 28
formula_hgc <- update(formula_main, hgc_28 ~ .)
did_hgc <- feols(formula_hgc, data = nlsy, weights = ~nlsy_weight,
                 cluster = ~senior_year)
summary(did_hgc)

# 5. Event-study graph -----------------------------------------------
nlsy[, rel_cohort := senior_year - 1982]     # 0 = class of 1982
event_df <- feols(enroll ~ i(rel_cohort, father_dead, ref = -1) +
                            post*father_dead + post + father_dead +
                            paste(controls, collapse=" + "),
                  data = nlsy, weights = ~nlsy_weight,
                  cluster = ~senior_year)

iplot(event_df, ref.line = 0) +
  labs(title = "Event-study: Orphan vs Non-orphan College Enrollment")

# 6. Robustness check: placebo cutoff (move policy to 1980) ----------
nlsy[, placebo_post := as.integer(senior_year >= 1980)]
placebo <- feols(enroll ~ father_dead*placebo_post + 
                           paste(controls, collapse=" + "),
                 data = nlsy, weights = ~nlsy_weight,
                 cluster = ~senior_year)
summary(placebo)
```
Comments:
• `father_dead*post` coefficient β̂ is the “effect of losing grant eligibility” (negative).  
• Standard errors clustered on graduating cohort (or state) capture serial correlation.

======================================================================
6. Expected Results
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Direction: Losing grant eligibility should reduce the probability of full-time college enrollment and lower completed schooling.

Magnitude priors (1980 dollars):  
– Average yearly benefit ≈ $6,700. If college sticker price elasticity is roughly −0.15 to −0.20, a $1,000 decrease in grants should lower enrollment by ~1.5–2 p.p.  
– Thus β̂_enroll ≈ −10–14 percentage points (6.7 × 1.5–2).  
– For years of schooling, one year ≈ 30 semester-hours; a 10 p.p. drop in enrollment may translate into ≈ −0.25 to −0.35 years of total completed schooling.

======================================================================
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DiD)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
C1: Pre-trend equality visually confirmed (event-study) ..................... 1  
C2: No anticipation/early response before 1982 ................................ 1  
C3: Composition of cohorts stable (no selective attrition) .................... 0.5  
C4: No concurrent orphan-specific shocks ...................................... 0.5  
C5: Treatment precisely timed and known ....................................... 1  
TOTAL (out of 5) ............................................................. 4.0

======================================================================
This plan delivers a transparent, replicable estimate of how the withdrawal of a large, unconditional grant program affected college-going and educational attainment in the early 1980s.
